_about: Hand transcription from the page images of Dreyer (ed.), Tychonis Brahe Dani Opera Omnia, vol. XII (1913 scan, archive.org operaomniaedidit12brahuoft), read by the agent on the images (not the OCR). Angles are degrees and minutes; Tycho's fractions of a minute are kept as written (1/6 = 10 arcsec, 1/3 = 20, 1/2 = 30, 2/3 = 40, 5/6 = 50). Times are Tycho's clock hours (H, M with fractions of a minute) counted from noon (vesperi) or midnight (mane), local apparent time as corrected by the observers. Dates are Julian (Denmark kept the Julian calendar until 1700). Confidence: H = the printed digits are unambiguous at full resolution; M = readable but a small fraction glyph; L = the observer or Dreyer flagged it, or the identification is inferred.

1595-10-25_vesperi.label: near opposition

Lucida Arietis.why: Tycho's own RA/Dec for 'Lucida [Aries]' on p.446 (Oct 16): 26 9 / 21 31 B; Hamal precessed to 1595 matches

Lucidum Latus Persei.why: Tycho gives its latitude 30 5 30 B and longitude 26 12 5/6 Taurus on p.447 (Oct 25 mane triangle); Mirfak

Oculus Tauri / Aldebaran.why: named 'Aldebaran' in the same page's footnote; RA 63 12 8, Dec 15 37 3/4 in Tycho's reduction

Vultur (occid.).why: clock star; the column is its hour angle west of the meridian read on the armillary (it advances 15 deg/hour; Altair never rises above 43 deg at Hven, so it cannot be an altitude)

Os Pegasi (or.).why: clock star in the 6 10 1/2 row, hour angle east

rows.note: Mars at 14 deg altitude, early in the night; the two declination readings differ by 2'; low weight, not used in the fit

1595-07-22_mane.label: far from opposition (Tycho: 'in [quadrature with the] Sun')

Markab (header: 'ab ore Peg.', reduction.why: The table header names Os Pegasi (Enif), but Enif lies about 71 deg from Mars that morning, not 50; Tycho's own reduction below the table uses 'Primae alae Peg.' with RA 341 9 1/4, Dec 13 3 37 B, which is alpha Peg precessed to 1595 (J2000 346.19, +15.21). Distance 50 28 fits Markab only. Header/reduction discrepancy noted.

Vultur (occid.).why: clock star, hour angle west; Tycho writes 'Resp. H.2 M.50' beside it
